subject: Which rows the Event List's `M`, `Position` and `Name` column headers are named by, read out of Logic's shipped binary
question: Three LabelSets carried one or two locales and named no Apple row. `derive_label_variants.py` answered `ambiguous` for all three -- 4, 7 and 18 rows carry those values. A row whose VALUE matches is not the row a control is NAMED by (`trackTypeMaster`'s best candidate is a Bass Amp label). Does the bundle decide it without a running Logic?

host.locale_note: Static reads of the shipped bundle; no Logic was running, so no UI locale was in play. en-US is recorded because the schema counts per-locale coverage by this exact string and the English row is the one cited.

reverify.expected: exit 0: 137 of 195 LabelSets name a row, and for each of the ten locales the corpus carries, AT LEAST ONE of that LabelSet's strings case-insensitively matches the value pinned for the row -- including eventListColumnM, eventListColumnPosition and eventListColumnName. Two things it does NOT check: `Scripts/check-labelsets-are-derived.py:149` folds case before comparing digests, so a member differing only in case still passes -- this is not an exact-identity check; and `:15-17` allows extras on purpose, so `variants` can carry tolerance Apple's data does not contain.
reverify.cost: ~10s; reads the committed canon index, launches nothing

method: Static reads only. Logic was NOT launched. (1) Every Base.lproj nib in Logic.framework was scanned for the class name `EventList`: 159 files, zero hits, so the columns are not built from a nib. (2) `nm -arch arm64` on Logic.framework's executable located `-[EventListView createTableColumns]` at 0x3fa468 and `-[EventListView columnTitle:forMenu:]` at 0x3f8c24. (3) `otool -arch arm64 -tvV` was dumped and the adrp/add pairs inside 0x3f8c24-0x3f9100 were reconstructed: the method references three `__DATA_CONST,__cfstring` objects at 0x2322ba0, 0x231fdc0 and 0x2316f20, each passed to what this reading identifies as a localization helper (a reading of the disassembly, not a re-derivation -- see limits) with a nil table against the bundle of `MAContentPackageManager` -- Logic.framework -- so the table is its own Localizable.strings. (4) Each of those three records was then READ: the 32-byte CFString struct followed into `__TEXT,__cstring` gives `M`, `Position` and `Name`. That corrects the first -- a co-reader had read it as `Muted`; `Muted` is a fourth cfstring at 0x2315880, held in x22 and stored one stack slot before the localized `M`. (5) The three rows were then read out of the pinned corpus in all ten locales and compared with what each LabelSet already carried.

canon.used_for: the row the Event List's mute header is titled from; nine locales spell it `M`
the same row in Simplified Chinese -- mute -- which is what separates it from MAMixer's `M`, whose zh_CN value stays `M`
the row the Event List's position header is titled from
the same row in Japanese; three of the seven rows carrying `Position` in English read 位置 here instead, so the value could not choose the row
the row the Event List's name header is titled from
the same row in Korean, which is the one locale this LabelSet already carried

observations.what: Base.lproj nibs in Logic.framework scanned for the class name EventList
rows in the bundle whose English value is `Name`
of those, rows sharing one ten-locale spelling
of those, rows whose Japanese reads 位置 rather than ポジション
of those, chord labels from ChordsKit rather than a mute column

conclusion: The Event List creates its columns in code. `-[EventListView columnTitle:forMenu:]` references three CFStrings -- `M`, `Position`, `Name` -- each matching a row this corpus pins in Logic.framework's own Localizable.strings; what this reading identifies as a localization call resolves each against that table (a reading, not a re-derivation -- see limits). Those three rows are now named in `derivedFrom` by eventListColumnM, eventListColumnPosition and eventListColumnName, which took them from one or two locales to ten. The mute column is the one that could not have been guessed: nine locales spell it `M` and Simplified Chinese spells it 静音, which is also what separates this row from MAMixer's `M` -- whose zh_CN value stays `M`. The Japanese position header is ポジション, not 位置, and three of the seven candidate rows would have given the wrong answer.
limits: Nothing here was read off a running Logic. What is proved is which key the shipped code looks up and what Apple pins at that key -- not that a Japanese Logic renders ポジション in that column on screen.

The instruction reading was done by a co-reader and has been re-derived here at four points: the two method addresses (nm), the three cfstring addresses being referenced inside the method (adrp/add reconstruction), the section those addresses live in, and -- added 2026-09-20 after review -- the cfstring CONTENTS, by following each record's data pointer into __TEXT,__cstring. That last step CORRECTED one of the three: 0x2322ba0 is `M`, not `Muted`. What is still a reading rather than a re-derivation is the identification of the callee at 0x9fd880 as a localization helper and of the bundle it resolves against as `MAContentPackageManager`'s.

`Muted` is the column identifier; the localization key for it is `M`. A rename of either in a later Logic breaks the binding, and NOTHING IN CI WOULD SHOW IT. `Scripts/check-labelsets-are-derived.py` compares the Swift LabelSets against the COMMITTED corpus index and never opens an installed Logic, so it keeps passing until somebody re-runs `Scripts/logic_canon.py build` against the new bundle and the row moves under it. An earlier version of this line said that guard failing would show the rename; it would not.
